One of the things that fascinamte me the most in writing (and other medium) is how some writers manage to develop characters so interesting in complex that you start thinking you might as well meet them around the corner. I'd like to learn how to do that too. I realize much of that comes from creativity, so, for starters it would be really helpful if someone could point me out to good works that could inspire this kind of idea. However, I also know that there is a lot of technique involved, and I was wondering if maybe someone could point me out to good books, manuals, tutorial, etc. where I can learn such skills.

Any help would be welcome, and it doesn't need to be restricted to writing, too. I would really benefit from knowledge into how to design characters visually too (for medium such as animations or games).

Thanks in advance!
A good way to learn character design?
Give characters at least one weakness. Let them make a mistake or two. Show that they have interests unrelated the story at hand, a hobby or something.
Thanks that's an interesting point to keep in mind!

Put the characters in situations that bring out the traits you find interesting about them, and, depending on how much comedic effect you're going for, exaggerate those traits to some extent.

Some writers like to fill out charts like this, but personally I think it makes more sense to start with a few basic characteristics for each character and work out the details if/when you need them.
ty =] I also like to kind of let my character develop "on it's own", but some planning may be useful. Thanks for the chart!

There are plausible characters and there are real characters. Forget writing for a moment and ask yourself, "When I'm describing someone else to someone else, do I do them justice? Am I really sitting behind their eyes, even a little bit? Or am I just superficially explaining them in terms of things they've done?" Be honest (to yourself) about how you answer this question.
